pr_title: Improve documentation and consistency of the `--commit` flag for `gh browse` command
pr_body:
This is a follow up PR to the discussion in #6926

Before, the --commit flag for the `gh browse` command always generated the `/tree` repository url for the latest commit.

This PR adjusts the `--commit` flag to match the `--branch` flag behavior. The `--commit` flag now accepts an arbitrary commit sha and generates the `/tree` url for the repository at that commit. It also defaults to the latest commit, if no argument is provided to the flag, to maintain backwards compatibility.

Fixes #6926 (maybe :laughing:)

issue_context.title: `gh browse -cn` should return the commit view not tree view
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

I want to get the URL for the latest commit (assuming it's pushed). I use `gh browse -cn` to get it in the terminal. It returns a "tree" URL and not a "commit" URL. This matters because I cannot view previous/next commits if I use this URL.

### Proposed solution

Return a "commit" link instead of a "tree" link. Example (tree -> commit):
- Current - `https://github.com/exemplar-codes/codevolution-nodejs/tree/dbe29aebea4d32343f6f12c2f8d6ab62157a9595`
- Goal - `https://github.com/exemplar-codes/codevolution-nodejs/commit/dbe29aebea4d32343f6f12c2f8d6ab62157a9595`

Or at least have an option that does this (if backward compatibility is a goal)

### Additional context
- [Feels like a missing feature - StackOverflow comment](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/69099079/how-to-get-github-latest-commit-url-using-cli-with-respect-to-current-branch/72876418?noredirect=1#comment132818486_72876418)
- On a GitHub text area, (like a comment, this issue), the two links are rendered differently. View here (pasted verbatim):
Tree: https://github.com/exemplar-codes/codevolution-nodejs/tree/dbe29aebea4d32343f6f12c2f8d6ab62157a9595
Commit: https://github.com/exemplar-codes/codevolution-nodejs/commit/dbe29aebea4d32343f6f12c2f8d6ab62157a9595
Adding a screenshot for the future:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48156230/215287817-5c6afd64-faae-4f1a-a281-e09cbda60c74.png)
comments: Also, the "commit link" described above opens much faster in the browser, compared to the "tree link".

@sanjarcode Thanks for writing in. Unfortunately, this is confusing behavior of this command and mostly due to the poor documentation of the `--commit` flag. If you want to get the commit link that you are after can use `gh browse SHA` using the SHA of the commit you want to view. Something like `gh browse $(git rev-parse HEAD)` will let you view the latest commit. 

I think to address this problem going forward we should update the `--commit` flag documentation to state that it opens the repository at the commit specified, defaulting to the latest commit.

Hi, I was gonna fix documentation on this but wanted to check with you first.

Looks like when the `--commit` flag is specified without a sha, the cli generates the "tree" url for the last commit:
```
❯ gh browse --commit --no-browser
https://github.com/cli/cli/tree/7d4ab65af3f7b28b1db760c3a730fadfacf24941
```
But if a commit sha is passed after the `--commit` flag, the cli generates the commit url:
```
❯ gh browse --commit 7d4ab65af3f7b28b1db760c3a730fadfacf24941 --no-browser
https://github.com/cli/cli/commit/7d4ab65af3f7b28b1db760c3a730fadfacf24941
```

Is this the expected behavior? Does passing a sha effectively overwrite the `--commit` flag?

@alex-petrov-vt I believe that is a bug/inconsistency in the command. If the `--commit` flag is passed it should always generate the `/tree/` URL. If the user wants the `/commit/` URL they do not need to pass any flags to the command just the SHA. Do you feel up to fixing that bug as well as the documentation?

@samcoe Sure, I can try to fix the inconsistency and improve the command docstring. Here's what I got so far: https://github.com/cli/cli/pull/7105. Please let me know if this is what you had in mind.

I do have another question though. Based on your previous comment:

> I think to address this problem going forward we should update the --commit flag documentation to state that it opens the repository at the commit specified, defaulting to the latest commit.

it sounds like the commit flag is maybe expected to accept a commit sha and generate the `/tree/` URL for the repository at that commit. That does not seem to be the current behavior. Right now, when the `--commit` flag is passed, the `/tree/` url is always generated for the current HEAD. Just wanted to double check that it's still the desired behavior.

@alex-petrov-vt You are correct, what I stated above on the current functionality was not exactly correct. I think we should update it along with the docs.

How I am envisioning the `browse` command working is that the `--commit` flag is equivalent to the `--branch` flag except for taking in commit SHA's instead of branch names. Right now the `--commit` flag is a boolean but I would suggest we change it to be a string flag. To maintain backwards compatibility, if the `--commit` flag is specified without a value, normally not allowed with string flags, we use the latest commit.

Then the docs for the `--commit` flag could say `Select another commit by passing in the commit SHA, default is the last commit`.

Does that make sense?

review_comments:
I couldn't think of a better way of maintaining backwards compatibility while switching the commit flag from a boolean flag to a string flag.

This seemed like a suggested way of doing it by the pflag: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/spf13/pflag#readme-setting-no-option-default-values-for-flags

However, this means that the commit flag now must use an equals sign to assign the flag value (i.e. `--commit=12a4`) which looks pretty inconsistent compared to the `--branch` flag, for example, which just expects a typical string argument after itself.

Please let me know if you think there's a way to improve this

Yeah this is unfortunately the only way to do this. I think it is good for now and then in a future release, perhaps when we do another major release, we can remove the `NoOptDefVal` and break the backwards compatibility.
